the momentum distribution of the matrix of lepton densities is distorted from the equilibrium distribution, since the modes with lower k << T are produced more efficiently than the higher ones.
the momentum dependence of densities is essential to determine the yields of sterile and active neutrinos and the baryon number asymmetry.
the momentum dependence of densities of leptonic fields is important to determine the yields of sterile and active neutrinos as well the baryon number density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
baryogenesis via the sterile neutrino oscillations.
the generation of the baryon (and lepton) asymmetry in the early Universe via sterile neutrino (flavor) oscillation in the framework of the νMSM.
the dynamics of sterile neutrino oscillations, which is the key to the baryogenesis in νMSM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism via sterile neutrino production is not viable for baryogenesis.
the momentum dependence is important and the most important mode is k 2 T for baryogenesis in νMSM.
baryogenesis via neutrino oscillation is a viable possibility in the framework of the νMSM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the baryogenesis via oscillation of sterile neutrino in the νMSSM is more efficient than the conventional one.
the momentum distribution of the matrix of leptonic densities is distorted significantly from the thermal equilibrium one, and the most important mode is k 2 T.
the baryogenesis via the sterile neutrino oscillations can be realized even if the sterile neutrinos are much heavier than the active neutrinos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the momentum distribution of the matrix of the densities of leptons plays a significant role in the baryogenesis in this model.
the momentum distribution of the matrix of the density of leptons is distorted significantly, and the baryon number density generated in the νMSSM is larger than that in the previous works.
the baryon yield per unit of the sterile neutrino mass is enhanced by about one order of magnitude compared with the previous result.
